note.text:
Length is the distance between two points. Its SI unit is the metre (m).
Other units: 1 km = 1000 m; 1 m = 100 cm; 1 cm = 10 mm (the same ladder as in Maths: km, hm, dam, m, dm, cm, mm).
Instruments:
• ruler or metre rule: lengths up to about 1 m; the smallest mark is 1 mm;
• measuring tape: long lengths, such as a room or a football field.
To measure with a ruler: put the start of the object on a mark (0 if you can), keep your eye straight above the mark, and if you did not start at 0, subtract: length = end − start.

cards.idea: Length is the distance between two points. SI unit: the metre (m). 1 km = {factor('km', 'm')} m, 1 m = {factor('m', 'cm')} cm, 1 cm = {factor('cm', 'mm')} mm.
example: Kumba to Mamfe is measured in km; a classroom in m; a pencil in cm; a grain of rice in mm.

cards.idea: Choose the instrument: a ruler for short lengths, a metre rule for about a metre, a measuring tape for long lengths.
example: The length of the classroom: a measuring tape.

cards.idea: On a ruler, the small marks are millimetres: there are {factor('cm', 'mm')} between two centimetre numbers.
example: This object is {l} mm long, that is {l / 10} cm.

questions.prompt: Convert this length: {up ? k / 10 : k * 10} {up ? p.a : p.b} = ? {up ? p.b : p.a}
questions.answer: up ? convertUnit(k / 10, p.a, p.b) : convertUnit(k * 10, p.b, p.a)

misconceptions.wrong: up ? convertUnit(k / 10, p.b, p.a) : convertUnit(k * 10, p.a, p.b)
misconceptions.explain: You went the wrong way. From a bigger unit to a smaller one, the number gets bigger; from smaller to bigger, it gets smaller.

solution: {up ? 'Multiply' : 'Divide'} by {factor(p.a, p.b)}: {up ? k / 10 : k * 10} {up ? p.a : p.b} = {answer} {up ? p.b : p.a}.

pick.why: For the length of a pencil, a ruler is best.
For the length of the classroom, a measuring tape is best.
For the width of your desk, a metre rule is best.
